body:
I think using Github is a great idea as it allows version tracking, distribution, pull requests and issues.

But, Github is not being used to its full potential.

The problem is using the Word document on Github as it is a binary file, no one can easily view the changes, etc.

I propose the ASVS content is developed in a plaintext format, possibly using Markdown. Each chapter or section can be in its own file.

This would allow the content to be easily viewed, modified and tracked.

For distribution of final versions, markdown to word/pdf/whatever converters can be used. Then adding the final touches to the converted document.

comments.body:
:+1: 
I've been experimenting with this on our own repos:
ASVS as JSON: https://github.com/ibuildingsnl/owasp-asvs/blob/master/src/asvs.json
Generated ReStucturedText: https://github.com/ibuildingsnl/owasp-aasvs/tree/master/docs
Read-the-docs version: http://owasp-aasvs.readthedocs.org/en/latest/

I really love RTD for this as they allow you to properly version the documents and export to PDF, though working with RST is a bit of a pain.

I disagree with the proposal. 

I don't think github is really useful in our case, I find it really intricate, IMHO as we are not tracking code changes github is kind of useless. Maybe we could just use github just to track proposed changes discussed in the mail list in form of ISSUES but just until they are integrated in the document (A sort of approved/agreed TODO)

I do like instead how we used google docs to finalize the version 3.0. 

An owner of the document can share a link to the current document and people will contribute adding suggestions as a tracked comments.  The owner of the document then will be able to accept/refuse proposed changes. 

I believe it's already enough complex as now to keep people involved, moving from a simple doc to a markdown doc, will increase the requirements to contribute, reducing then the possibility to involve people. 

IMHO google docs provides all of what we need.

Just to add some merit to Github being a valuable writing tool;

Github have their own 'showcase' page highlighting the usefulness of the service in book writing (https://github.com/showcases/writing). Giving examples of projects using the service for this purpose. Here is one example: https://github.com/SamyPesse/How-to-Make-a-Computer-Operating-System

Other services using Git (or some other version control system) specifically for writing are also available such as:

https://www.gitbook.com/
https://www.penflip.com/

From what I have seen, version control for writing is becoming more and more popular as writers (mainly technical at the moment) see the benefits of using version control and plaintext for their writing. For example, DHH, the author of Ruby on Rails, wrote his Rework book in Textmate.

Currently, the binary doc file is being tracked on Github as a binary file as well as using Google Docs. IMO it would be much simpler to consolidate everything on to Github.

I don't think Github should be dismissed simply because it was designed for source code. After all, source code is based on the written language. But of course, there are other reasons why it could be dismissed.

It is a big change and it will affect those with more involvement in the project than me but I think it is worth considering.

I have to say that I was not aware of gitbook and penflip. Now that I know
these tools, I have to withdraw my previous position.

I agree that with gitbook/penflip availability we should convert the doc to
a markdown document and use a "binary" form only at the end to deliver the
standard.

boos @ http://boos.core-dumped.info

95% of the work we do is in tables, and these tables aren't easy. Google
docs really struggled with them, and I doubt markdown, which has ultra
basic tables, could cope.

Nearly 100% of the results are in Word or PDF downloads.

I think the next time we do a major update, the way that worked best to
collaborate was to use a Google Doc, but it was HORRIBLE at producing a
good looking PDF or reasonable HTML format that could be consumed. Also,
right now, we are at the very upper limit of the length of document that
Google Docs can handle. It was terrible at editing with many of us going at
it.

We are working on making a more computer consumable version of the ASVS
available sooner or later, but first I want to get the translations on the
go.

Andrew

Here is an example Markdown table for those interested, to show that it is possible, but I'm not sure how this would scale or if it would meet the complexities needed.

Rendered by Github:

| Tables | Are | Cool |
| --- | :-: | --: |
| col 1 is | left-aligned | $1600 |
| col 2 is | centered | $12 |
| col 3 is | right-aligned | $1 |

Code used for the above:

```
| Tables   |      Are      |  Cool |
|----------|:-------------:|------:|
| col 1 is |  left-aligned | $1600 |
| col 2 is |    centered   |   $12 |
| col 3 is | right-aligned |    $1 |
```

Here is an example table using the ASVS format:

| # | Description | 1 | 2 | 3 | Since |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 3.1 | Verify that there is no custom session manager, or that the custom session manager is resistant against all common session management attacks. | Yes | Yes | Yes | 1.0 |
| 3.2 | Verify that sessions are invalidated when the user logs out. | Yes | Yes | Yes | 1.0 |
| 3.3 | Verify that sessions timeout after a specified period of inactivity. | Yes | Yes | Yes | 1.0 |
| 3.4 | Verify that sessions timeout after an administratively-configurable maximum time period regardless of activity (an absolute timeout). | No | Yes | Yes | 1.0 |
| 3.5 | Verify that all pages that require authentication have easy and visible access to logout functionality. | Yes | Yes | Yes | 1.0 |

My final comment, sorry for spamming ;)

Here is the latest ASVS converted to Markdown using the word-to-markdown Ruby gem:

https://github.com/ethicalhack3r/owasp-asvs-markdown/blob/master/asvs.md

I removed the images as they were not showing in Github and were large (the gem converted images to base64 data images). See commit history: https://github.com/ethicalhack3r/owasp-asvs-markdown/commits/master

This is just a PoC to show that it is possible.

The SKF project has a copy of the ASVS in Markdown format, which will provide an API version of the ASVS. 

https://github.com/blabla1337/skf-flask
I still believe managing the ASVS in markdown makes much more sense than docx files but respect your decision

Based on the discussion above, the factors chosen in the selection of tool for maintaining ASVS seem to be as follows:
1. Support for complex tabular information - "95% of the work we do is in tables, and these tables aren't easy. Google docs really struggled with them, and I doubt markdown, which has ultra basic tables, could cope.". Can we please have some examples of these tables?
2. Ability to export to PDF and HTML - "but it was HORRIBLE at producing a
good looking PDF or reasonable HTML format that could be consumed"

I would like to introduce the following factors in the decision analysis that are generally important to the health of any Open Source project:
1. Making it easy for contributors - reviewers as well as content contributors - in order to encourage more people to contribute to ASVS
2. Easy and granular traceability of changes to the standard
3. Avoiding duplication of effort and fragmentation in the form of new repositories which are a copy of ASVS just in another format

Can we please have a formal "Decision Analysis and Resolution" on this?

title: Changing to Markdown
